content:
Let the side length of each large square be \(2\), so each square has area \(4\).

### Square I
The diamond has diagonals of length \(2\), so its area is
\[
\frac{2\cdot 2}{2}=2.
\]
The inner square’s vertices are the midpoints of the diamond’s sides. Its side length is \(1\), so its area is \(1\). Therefore,
\[
S_I=2-1=1.
\]

### Square II
Take the bottom-left corner as \((0,0)\). The other vertices of the shaded triangle are the top midpoint \((1,2)\) and the right midpoint \((2,1)\). Thus,
\[
S_{II}
=\frac12\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\right|
=\frac12|1-4|
=\frac32.
\]

### Square III
The shaded triangle has base \(2\) and height \(2\), so
\[
S_{III}=\frac12(2)(2)=2.
\]

Hence,
\[
1<\frac32<2,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\text{B: }S_I<S_{II}<S_{III}}.
\]
